name: International Protection (asylum)

qualifying_event.description: Available to foreign nationals meeting the criteria for refugee status, subsidiary protection, or temporary protection under EU law and Estonian legislation.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Evidence of persecution, serious harm, or a qualifying mass-displacement situation (e.g. the EU temporary protection mechanism for Ukraine).

requirements.blocker_text: Requires meeting the criteria for refugee status or subsidiary protection under EU and Estonian law, assessed via a border, accelerated, or substantive procedure depending on the case.

evidence_required.document: Application submitted at a border crossing point or a PBGB service point (Northern Prefecture, Tallinn, for applicants already in Estonia)

outcome.duration_length: temporary residence permit valid up to 5 years

sources.title: Police and Border Guard Board of Estonia (politsei.ee) -- Applying for asylum: international protection

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Estonia's initial build. Unlike Barbados' bb_asylum (which is a 'never existed' closed case), Estonia has a real, EU-framework-compliant domestic asylum system with three procedure types: border procedure (up to 12 weeks, for weak claims or security risks), accelerated procedure (up to 3 months, for likely-unfounded claims), and substantive procedure (up to 6 months, the standard full assessment). work_rights is set 'restricted' as a common default for asylum seekers/protection holders across this dataset pending a confirmed source on exact employment rights, which the page fetched in this pass did not address. leads_to_pr (60 months, matching the 5-year residence permit) and leads_to_citizenship are inferred from this route's outcome feeding into the same long-term-residence and naturalisation tracks as any other legal residence in Estonia, not from a source stating this specifically for protection holders -- flagged as an inference, not a confirmed fact. Family members of a protection beneficiary may apply for residence permits valid until the beneficiary's own permit expires, confirmed at tier-1.
